title: fix: reduce Gateway memory retained after restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway with many sessions keeps prepared restart-recovery rows after recovery finishes. Published admission callbacks retain the startup scope, which still references the completed recovery closure and its parsed rows.

The source chain is `session-entry-json.ts:30` (decode), `session-restart-resume-discovery.ts:72` (prepare descriptive rows), `session-restart-resume.ts:357` (capture prepared stores), and `agent-database-startup.ts:582` (retain recovery in the startup scope).

## User Impact

Completed restart recovery releases its temporary session data. Recovery ordering, readiness, failure handling, and session behavior remain unchanged. This is a retention fix; it does not claim to explain all long-running Gateway memory growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clear `preparation.recoverInputs` in the existing settlement `finally`, before releasing input waiters (`src/state/agent-database-startup.ts:662`). No cache, interning table, config, schema, or dependency change. Reuse the existing equivalent synchronous assertion helper to keep the startup owner below its line cap, and include that helper in the PR wrapper's extracted-source inventory.

Production delta: **−2 runtime lines**; the inventory entry is +1 (net −1 including tooling); tests: +39.

## Evidence

The real-owner collection regression fails on unchanged parent `b4254cb2f6fa66805de3bfe0867a077ba7326efc` for both successful and failed recovery. It passes with the fix while the published admission callback remains alive. **84 owner/consumer tests across five files pass. Independent Codex autoreviews are scoped-clean through P2.**

### Synthetic Gateway A/A/B

Each arm restores the same pristine **35.015 GiB agent database**, with 10,800 sessions, 4,300 settled restart candidates, 65 clients, 20 concurrent mock-provider runners, 40 plugins, 512 skills, and 62,000 workspace files (~1.1 GB). After normal Doctor preparation and a one-minute warmup, each runs ten measured minutes of list/history/events/appends/tools traffic. All three pass the workload validator: required RPCs, zero recorded RPC errors, matched tool calls/results, timestamp writes, and Prometheus scrapes.

| Measurement | A1 unchanged | A2 unchanged | B fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Retained snapshot, MB | 596.186 | 595.308 | 582.263 |
| Duplicate-string potential, MB | 36.148 | 36.144 | 28.512 |
| Excess string copies | 722,034 | 722,332 | 571,768 |
| Completed recovery graph, MB | 14.049 | 14.027 | absent |
| Sampled allocation, MB/s | 59.22 | 61.51 | 62.58 |
| Main-thread CPU | 15.68% | 16.23% | 16.81% |
| Session admission, ms | 119.7 | 134.1 | 122.1 |
| Completed turns / tool calls / tool results | 200 / 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 / 200 |
| Timestamp writes / history reads | 102 / 307 | 104 / 314 | 101 / 330 |
| sessions.list p50 / p99, ms | 5.53 / 43.10 | 6.02 / 34.24 | 6.44 / 42.22 |
| chat.history p50 / p99, ms | 11.35 / 46.69 | 13.77 / 46.31 | 14.00 / 119.95 |

MB is decimal. The fix saves **13.04–13.92 MB retained** and **7.63 MB duplicate potential**, beyond A/A spreads of 0.879 MB and 0.004 MB respectively. About 150,000 excess string copies disappear. The largest four flat-string groups are repeated workspace paths: approximately 1.818 MB each before and 1.302 MB each after. The recovery graph also holds repeated IDs and type values.

CPU and allocation are modestly higher in B, with increments comparable to A/A variation and a different number of history reads; no CPU, allocation-rate, or latency improvement is claimed. The repeatable result is lower retention. The fixture runs on APFS and does not establish btrfs behavior.

Allocation sampling includes collected objects at a 512 KiB interval. Timing and sampling stop before forced GC and the harness's settled heap capture. Canonical `heap-snapshot-diff.mjs --summary --labels` uses reviewed source labels; duplicate accounting covers complete flat strings shorter than 1,024 characters and excludes truncated longer groups. An earlier independent A/A/B on the same session/workspace shape with a 451 MiB database used `diagnostics.heapSnapshot` after ten minutes and found the same owner, with 13.01–15.27 MB retained savings.

### Checks and investigated failures

**Exact-head CI [44031349532](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44031349532) is green for `c296556147649ea4889cf8c3e6674c7fa5c30e7d`. ClawSweeper's review of that head has zero findings/open items.**

Initial CI caught a PR-caused missing assertion-helper entry in the wrapper inventory. Commit `c296556147649` fixes it. The repaired inventory passes 24 closure tests and 17 provisioning tests locally; one Linux-only case is skipped on macOS. One additional macOS cold/warm/sparse sibling-checkout test exceeds 120 seconds on both candidate and exact unchanged parent. Its causal performance-regression commit is not established; it remains an investigated local timeout, not a claimed pass or inherited-CI waiver. No timeout or ignore rule changed.

`pnpm check:changed` ran. The initial candidate line-cap finding was fixed and the focused ratchet passes. Format, lint, typechecks, schema and other guards pass. Three unrelated dead-export failures reproduce on the exact parent and are recorded as main regressions for repair:

- `approval-shared.ts:isApprovalRecordVisibleToClient`: #200360 (`ff2cb7e86274c`) removed its last production barrel consumer.
- `spawn-broker/host.ts:BrokerNativeResourceLease`: #200370 (`df78722789e09`) changed its re-export while extracting the host contract.
- `system-agent/operation-types.ts:SystemAgentPluginCapabilityReview`: #200392 (`b0d95fd4a9d6a`) added the exported type and inline import-type consumer reported unused by the canonical checker.

No baseline/exclusion changes and no failed-CI exception are used for landing.
